learning: If slalom progress passes 0.18 and oval oscillation stays near 0.3, the inertia lever works and body length can stay at 0.10 m. If the s-bend drops below 0.6 or the oval falls below 18 finishes, return body_length to 0.14 m. If slalom stays at 0.17 to 0.18 with max_error near 0.06, the stall is controller reaction time and should be reported as a controller-side limit.
notes: Complete robot for the Builder's body_length 0.10 m proposal, with mass 0.6 kg and all other values as iteration 8. The controller is identical to iteration 8, so body length is the only change. Sensor weights stay proportional to x and are independent of mass and body length.
rationale: Iteration 8 (417.9, best) used wheel_radius 0.040 m, wheel_track 0.10 m, mass 0.6 kg, and five sensors at y=0.08 m with a 0.012 m footprint. Iteration 9 showed that mass 0.5 kg hurt the oval (18/20) and s-bend (0.521), and the slalom stayed at 0.165, so mass returns to 0.6 kg. The Builder's one change is body_length 0.14 to 0.10 m, which cuts yaw inertia by about 28 percent through (L^2+W^2) at the same mass. Sensing, drivetrain and controller are kept at the iteration 8 values, so the body length is the only variable against that baseline. Because the slalom has held at progress 0.16 to 0.18 under every sensing and track change, this is the first test of the turn-response lever. The controller is unchanged (base_speed 1.7, kp 2.5, ki 0.05, kd 0.4, weights -2 to +2 proportional to x, last_direction), since mass and body length do not change the signal scale. Expected from the Builder: slalom progress above 0.2, s-bend at or above 0.6, oval at 18 or more finishes. The Integrator's risk is faster yaw response adding oval oscillation, which iteration 8 already had at 0.31.
